rootNote: Teaching roots chosen from WLC counts (OSHB 3d15126, verb tokens by Strong's number incl. suffixed forms): subtype I-Waw: H3427 יָשַׁב, 1070 tokens (Qal 1024, Hiphil 36, Niphal 7, Hophal 2, Piel 1), the most frequent I-Waw root with no second weakness and the paradigm root of GKC Paradigm K and Davidson §39. יָלַד (489; 8 stems) is attested in more stems and supplies most derived-stem examples; ישב is kept as teaching root because it is the root all three grammars print. Subtype I-Yod: H3190 יָטַב, 112 tokens (Hiphil 69, Qal 43), the most frequent true I-Yod root and the root of GKC Paradigm L and K&J's I-Yod columns. More frequent roots with initial י (יָצָא 1059, יָלַךְ 1040, יָדַע 936) have a second weakness or are הלך-type; see the VERIFY file.
source: Forms from GKC §§69-71 + Paradigms K and L (PDF p. 481) and Davidson, Introductory Hebrew Grammar §39 paradigm (pp. 178-179), both in /workspace/hebrew-books/ and read from page images. Squares those books do not print but K&J, Learning Biblical Hebrew pt. 2, I-Waw/Yod Verb Chart (pp. 339-340) prints are formBasis 'printed'. Piel/Pual/Hitpael and the remaining squares follow the strong-verb.json pattern with the radicals substituted (formBasis 'rule'). Not copied from any copyrighted chart.
verificationMethod: Each form was matched (consonants + vowel points, accents ignored, dagesh lene and plene/defective ḥolem, shureq and ḥireq-yod spellings normalized) against OSHB morphhb-wlc tokens with the same OSHB morph slot. The 2nd and 3rd radicals are positional (ש ב / ט ב); everything else, including the first radical's ו/י/absence, must agree letter for letter. The example root was checked against its Strong's headword (initial י, same R2 R3) and the subtype list (true I-Yod roots H3190 H3243 H3364 H3474 H3231 H3001; everything else is original I-Waw). Ketiv excluded. Imperatives may carry paragogic ה; infinitives construct may carry a preposition. Example preference: teaching root of the subtype, then another root of the same subtype; each in order no prefix, ו, preposition. Every matched token was cross-checked against STEPBible TAHOT; tokens where TAHOT disagrees are never used as examples.

notes.subtypes: Two subtypes share this file (field 'subtype'). 'I-Waw' (teaching root ישב) fills all 207 squares. 'I-Yod' (teaching root יטב) adds only the squares where true I-Yod verbs differ: Qal imperfect, wayyiqtol, imperative and infinitives, and all of Hiphil. Each cell has a unique 'key' = subtype/id.
notes.iYodRoots: True I-Yod roots (GKC §70 Rem. 1): יטב, ינק, יקץ, ישׁר, ילל (Hiphil), ימן (Hiphil), and יבשׁ in Qal (its Hiphil הוֹבִישׁ follows I-Waw). All other י-initial roots are original I-Waw.
notes.yirashType: Most original I-Waw verbs keep a quiescent י in the Qal imperfect with a-vowel, like ירשׁ: יִירַשׁ, imperative רֵשׁ/יְרַשׁ, infinitive רֶשֶׁת (GKC §69; Davidson p. 178). Only a small group of verbs drops the first radical like יֵשֵׁב. Note only; such roots never serve as examples for the ישב-type Qal imperfect squares because the vowels differ.
notes.assimilating: יצק / יצר / יצת / יצג / יצע (and נצב / יצב) assimilate the first radical like a nun in some forms: יִצֹּק, יִצַּת, הִצִּית, הִצִּיג, הִתְיַצֵּב (GKC §71). Roots with צ as second radical are therefore never used as examples. Note only.
notes.halak: הָלַךְ behaves like an I-Waw verb of the ישב type: יֵלֵךְ, וַיֵּלֶךְ, לֵךְ, לֶכֶת, Hiphil הוֹלִיךְ (GKC §69; OSHB files those forms under H3212 יָלַךְ). Note only; never an example root.
notes.yakol: יָכֹל has the irregular imperfect יוּכַל (GKC §69). Never an example root.
notes.piel: Piel, Pual and Hitpael are regular, with י as first radical (יִלֵּד, יֻלַּד, הִתְיַלֵּד). Built by rule from strong-verb.json.
notes.fsParticiple: fs participles: -ֶת type main by the standing ruling; K&J's -ָה forms are printed alternates.
